t: Three villages on the Hooghly became the English East India Company's settlement from 1690, and after the Company's victory at Plassey in 1757 Calcutta was the centre of its rule in Bengal.
As the capital of British India until 1911 it grew into the second largest city of the British Empire after London and was the home of the Bengal Renaissance and of the early nationalist movement.
The famine of 1943, the communal violence of 1946 and the Partition of 1947 changed its population, and later decades brought economic decline and then recovery.
dyk: The Calcutta High Court ruled in 2003 that Job Charnock, long believed to be the founder of Calcutta, was not its founder, and that the city therefore has no birthday.
ev: Job Charnock returns to Sutanuti and hoists the Company standard on the bank of the Hooghly
Siraj ud-Daulah captures Calcutta and Fort William
The Company defeats the Nawab at Plassey, and Calcutta becomes the centre of its power in Bengal
A cyclone strikes the city and kills about 60,000 people
The capital of British India moves from Calcutta to New Delhi
Millions starve in the Bengal famine
The partition of India and of Bengal sends hundreds of thousands of Hindus into the city
The city's official name changes from Calcutta to Kolkata

f.founded: The recorded history of the city began in 1690 with the arrival of the English East India Company. Job Charnock is often regarded as the founder, but in 2003 the Calcutta High Court ruled that the city has no founder.
f.where: On the eastern bank of the Hooghly River in the lower Ganges Delta, in West Bengal, India, about 80 km west of the border with Bangladesh.
f.known: The Company settlement of Calcutta; the siege of 1756 and the Black Hole; the Battle of Plassey; capital of British India until 1911; the Bengal Renaissance; the University of Calcutta; the nationalist movement; the Partition of 1947
f.today: Kolkata is the capital of the Indian state of West Bengal and the largest city of eastern India.
